evals.name: deletes-class-a-restatement
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The uncommitted diff contains one code file whose comments restate the adjacent lines: a '// increment counter' above 'counter++;' and a commented-out block of dead code. The file has no other comments.)
expectations: Classifies both comments as class A (zero information) and deletes them outright
Does not modify any non-comment code in the file
Reports per-file counts of applied class-A deletions
Does not commit; leaves the edits in the working tree for review

evals.name: proposes-class-b-without-test-net
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The uncommitted diff contains a code file where a comment narrates what a 6-line block does — a class-B extract-function candidate. The repository has no discoverable test command: no test script in the package manifest, no Makefile target, no ecosystem default that resolves.)
expectations: Classifies the block comment as class B with Extract Function as the named move
Does NOT apply the refactoring or delete the comment, because no runnable test net was discovered
Emits the class-B treatment as a proposal in the report
Does not treat the presence of a linter as a substitute for tests

evals.name: never-touches-exempt-surfaces
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The uncommitted diff contains: a public exported function with a JSDoc block, a file-top license header, a line with '// eslint-disable-next-line', a 'TODO(#412): remove after migration' marker, a terse '// items must stay sorted; binary search depends on it' constraint comment, and a change inside .github/workflows/ci.yml.)
expectations: Leaves the public-API JSDoc, license header, lint directive, and TODO(#412) marker untouched
Keeps the sorted-items constraint comment as a class-C keep and says why in the report
Never edits the .github/workflows/ file — excluded path dropped at scoping time
Refuses to reinterpret 'remove comments' as deleting the class-C or exempt material

evals.name: stages-narrative-before-deletion

evals.name: applies-local-move-without-test-net
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The uncommitted diff contains a TypeScript file where '// milliseconds since epoch' sits above 'const t = Date.now();' and 't' is used three times in the same function and nowhere else. The repository has no discoverable test command. The tooling probe reports tree-sitter present for typescript.)
expectations: Classifies the comment as class B with Rename Variable as the named move
APPLIES the rename (to a name such as 'millisecondsSinceEpoch') and deletes the comment despite the absence of a test net, because Rename Variable on a function-local identifier creates no interface
Runs the change-shape check on the edit and cites its RENAME-ONLY verdict with the identifier mapping in the report
Reports the item as applied, not proposed, and does not ask for a test suite it already knows is absent

evals.name: reverts-when-ast-proof-fails
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The uncommitted diff contains a class-B Rename Variable candidate: '// retry budget in attempts' above 'let n = 3;' where n is function-local. When the rename is applied, the change-shape check reports CODE-CHANGED with kinds=['number'] because the edit also altered a neighbouring numeric literal from 3 to 5 instead of returning RENAME-ONLY.)
expectations: Runs the change-shape check after applying the move, before deleting the comment
On CODE-CHANGED, reverts the move so the file matches its pre-edit content, and restores the comment
Demotes the item to a proposal and quotes the change-shape verdict, including which token kinds differed
Leaves no partially applied edit in the working tree

evals.name: never-deletes-discovered-machine-marker
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The repository ships scripts/check-quiet-exits.sh, a CI gate that greps hook scripts for the annotation '# quiet-exit-ok: <reason>'. The uncommitted diff contains a hook script with the line 'command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0 # quiet-exit-ok: sink is fire-and-forget' and, elsewhere in the same file, '# increment the counter' above 'count=$((count + 1))'. The marker is not in any universal pragma list.)
expectations: Runs marker discovery before triage and locates the gate's matcher in scripts/check-quiet-exits.sh rather than guessing the marker's spelling
Treats 'quiet-exit-ok' as a repo-local machine-read marker: exempt, never classified, never deleted
Deletes only the restating '# increment the counter' comment
The report names the discovered marker family and the file that consumes it, so the reader can see what was protected and why

evals.name: does-not-treat-heredoc-body-as-comments
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The uncommitted diff contains a shell test script that writes a fixture with cat >"$F" <<'EOF' whose body includes the lines '# used to buffer; now flushes' and '# as you asked, retry three times', followed by EOF. Above a later command the script has a real restating comment '# print the result' over 'echo "$result"'. The tooling probe reports pygments present.)
expectations: Does not classify, count, or delete any line inside the heredoc body, because those lines are string data the script writes, not comments
Deletes the restating '# print the result' comment
The per-file count in the report excludes the heredoc lines
The report states which tooling layer read the file (pygments or tree-sitter), not a line-prefix grep

evals.name: reports-degraded-tooling-layer
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The tooling probe reports pygments absent, tree-sitter absent, and scc absent. The uncommitted diff contains a shell script with two heredocs and a Python module with a docstring and one restating comment.)
expectations: Runs the tooling probe at scope time and reports the layer the run is operating at
Refuses the apply path on the shell file at grep precision and says why: a line-prefix read cannot distinguish heredoc bodies from comments
For each absent layer, names the specific capability lost in install-hint shape rather than a generic 'consider installing'
Does not silently proceed as if it had parser-level precision

evals.name: keeps-rejected-alternative-rationale
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:dissolve-comments

(The uncommitted diff contains a guard script whose header says 'git branch -D is deliberately NOT blocked: a deleted branch is reflog-recoverable' and 'the helper is deliberately not named dirname, which would shadow the real command for every sourced guard'. Neither sentence has a referent in the adjacent code. The same file has '# increment counter' above 'count=$((count + 1))'.)
expectations: Classifies both header sentences as class C negative information (what the code deliberately does not do, and why an alternative was rejected) and keeps them
Does not treat 'no referent in the adjacent code' as evidence of class A; recognizes that an absence claim cannot be restated by code that is not there
Deletes the '# increment counter' restatement
The report explains the negative-information reasoning for the keeps in one line each
